text:
dave_acme_pm: Hey team — our customers started seeing 500s from /v1/rerank today. Happens when input contains emojis and we suspect embedded null bytes. Example payload attached below. Request-id: req_02ZXY. Can someone advise a quick workaround?

omar_support: Sorry about that, thanks for the details. Can you paste a minimal repro body (no PII) and which SDK/language you're using? Also the timestamp of the failed request if you have it.

dave_acme_pm: Minimal repro (Node):
```js
const body = {
  queries: ["Best result for \u0000\ud83d\ude0a"],
  candidates: ["A\u0000\uFEFF thing", "Another text 😊"]
};
// POST to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
```
Error we see: 500 Internal Server Error, and in logs: "utf8_decode_error at pos=8".

omar_support: Got it. Can you try replacing nulls client-side as temporary workaround? e.g. `.replace(/\u0000/g, '')` before sending. Also, if you're sending raw bytes from some older service, make sure JSON is valid UTF-8 (UTF-8 must not contain lone surrogates).

jess_engineer: digging in. Quick summary: our rerank validation path rejects inputs that are not valid UTF-8 or contain C0/C1 control chars we don't allow. Null bytes (\u0000) are a special-case that can cause the tokenizer / KV layers to choke. Log excerpt: `ValueError: Invalid UTF-8 sequence at byte 12 (\u0000 encountered) -> rejecting request`

liam_ml: additional nuance — some tokenizers treat surrogate pairs incorrectly when broken across bytes; emojis encoded as lone surrogates (e.g., from bad UTF-16 -> UTF-8 conversion) will fail downstream.

omar_support: Short-term fixes: 1) sanitize `.replace(/\u0000/g, '')` 2) normalize with NFKC and strip control chars: `text = text.normalize('NFKC').replace(/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]/g, '')` 3) ensure clients send JSON encoded as UTF-8 (Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8).

dave_acme_pm: Tried (1) and (2) — it stops the 500s. Thanks. Any plan for server-side handling? We have a bunch of clients; cleaning all of them is non-trivial.

jess_engineer: We're going to add a server-side sanitizer as a safety net for the next patch: it will reject requests with clearly invalid byte sequences with a 400 and a helpful error instead of 500, and optionally strip nulls for customers on hosted tier. Opening PR and a migration note.

liam_ml: Also adding an eval to ensure scores aren't silently corrupted by sanitizer (we'll run a small regression on rerank output distribution after stripping nulls).

omar_support: For tracking: I've created a ticket (SUP-4892) and linked the request id req_02ZXY. Workaround documented in the ticket.

deploy_bot: deploy queued: infra/sanitizer-proxy #345 -> staging, estimated window 30m. :rocket:

jess_engineer: follow-up: if anyone hits 422 instead of 500, that means JSON was syntactically valid but contained lone surrogate halves — we will return a clearer `invalid_utf8` field in the response body after the fix.

dave_acme_pm: Great, we'll hold off mass rollout of client fit until we see the staging patch. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
